claim: On neutral_hostile_v1/09_ml_artifacts, reconstructing the exact same DGO1 delimiter record into one contiguous logical output buffer with gifted NumPy vector scatter reduces delimiter inverse wall time by 85.6% versus the canonical Python inverse, while preserving byte-for-byte output and archive integrity.

decision.reason: The predecessor block/strided-slice oracle retained 45,979 per-segment Python buffers and recovered only ~5.2%. Eliminating that ownership layout and scattering directly into one contiguous output recovers ~85.6% of inverse wall time. This is strong causal evidence that Python object/layout work, not the DGO1 grammar or Zstd payload itself, owns most of the remaining delimiter inverse cost on this substrate.
decision.promotion_boundary: NumPy is gifted only as an oracle engine and is not a CMPCT core dependency. This result grants no product or release credit. Productization requires a dependency-appropriate implementation (preferably native/shared or a standard-library exact fast path), then complete-product runtime, memory, integrity, recovery, native/platform and release gates on one exact candidate.
decision.next_question: Can a dependency-free standard-library strided scatter, or the shared native core, realize a material fraction of this single-buffer headroom without adding global carrying cost?

scope: One-record, one-workload research oracle. It proves addressable implementation headroom, not product runtime or release readiness.
